caustic-web.look: Closed net of thin bright curved lines around dark soft-floored cells, with faint secondary folds crossing the cell floors and line brightness that varies along each edge. Next to a forward ray histogram of the same height it is the same picture at Depth up to about 1.1. What it lacks against the truth at Depth 1.6 and up: the truth has wide two-edged ribbons and cusped bowties where the web draws a single crisp line. The wide view at 16 px per unit breaks into dots because the lines are thinner than a pixel. Relief view is spiky and is not a terrain.
caustic-web.dims: 2D measured. 3D measured in two forms: plane (w3=0, z is a parameter of the height, lens stays xy; same look as 2D, morphs smoothly, corr .88 to .91 against truth across z) and true 3D lens (w3=1, 3x3 det; slices stay a net with extra loops and rounder cells). 4D measured only with a 16-wave height on the GenTileable torus mapping: the net holds, no seams in a 2x2 repeat, a bit busier with faint arcs in cell floors. No 4D Simplex kernel was built.
caustic-web.range: -0.772..1.000 over 8 seeds and offsets, mean -0.513. Upper bound 1 is analytic, lower bound depends on Depth and was measured.
caustic-web.artifacts: Lines alias below about 30 px per unit at eps 0.08; raise eps at small Feature Scale. Depth above about 1.6 stays a clean net rather than turning into overlapping ribbons, so it departs from the true image (corr .74 at 1.6, .46 at 2.4) while still looking good. Auto damp removed the grain and rings that fixed damp 0.7 showed from Depth 1.25 up; nothing grainy seen to Depth 3.
caustic-web.node_shape: CausticWeb : ScalableGenerator, Seeded, VariableRange. Depth (hybrid float, 1.1), Steps (int, 3; 0 gives the single-sheet form), Line Softness eps (float, 0.08), Gamma (float, 0.5), Field enum {Gradient = pool light closed cells, Free = independent noises, silk filaments}, Lens Dims enum {Full, XY Only}. Step factor is derived per lane from Depth, not exposed.
caustic-web.port_notes: Straight-line maths and a constant loop count; a per-lane step factor is fine with a hybrid Depth. Needs internal Simplex with analytic gradient and Hessian in 2D, 3D, 4D (simplex2h and simplex3h are written from the kernel formula and were checked against the truth histogram). Output is Sqrt( eps / ( Abs(det) + eps ) ) * 2 - 1, so no Pow at the default gamma. Avoid Perlin as the height: it shows axis streaks even in the true histogram. Plane waves work but cost more: scalar 336 ns at 8 waves, 574 ns at 12, against 233 ns for Simplex. There is a kink at det=0 only: max|dv| falls 0.665, 0.086, 0.012 for h = 1e-3, 1e-4, 1e-5, so it is continuous with a very steep slope (677 per unit), which is why c0ratio reads 2 rather than 8.
caustic-web.params_text: D=1.1,M=3,eps=0.08,gamma=0.5,hgt=2,fq=0.8 (auto damp 1/(1+0.6D)); M=2 as the economy setting

critic.params: D=1.1,M=3,eps=0.08,gamma=0.5,hgt=2,fq=0.8 (auto damp 1/(1+0.6D)); M=2 is a 23% cheaper economy setting with a near identical picture
critic.notes: The win is on look, not cost: estimated AVX2 cost (not ported) is about the same as the graph rival. Metric caveat: corr and IoU after a 1.5 px blur reward wide ribbons, so differences under about 0.02 and any win by a speckled candidate mean nothing; the eye must decide. Known flaws: kink at det=0 (max slope 677), lines alias below about 30 px per unit and the 4x wide view is dots, relief is spiky and not a terrain, Depth above 1.6 departs from the true ribbons and bowties. Port risk: needs an internal Simplex with analytic gradient and Hessian in 2D, 3D and 4D, and the 4D kernel is unwritten.
critic.improved: Tried a regularised Newton back map and Picard-then-Newton polish (added as cand newton / picnewt in t_caustic_compare.cpp, prev saved as .prev.cpp). Picard+Newton scored higher than web/3 (corr .926 IoU .62 vs .921 .53) but the image is worse: speckled double edges and debris at junctions, because the polish lands on both sides of the fold. Gentler settings are cleaner but score lower (.87 to .91). web/4 equals web/3 (.920 vs .921), so Picard at 3 steps is saturated. Nothing changed in the gallery defaults. The chain-rule soft form (M=4, step 0.5) re-scored .931/.62 at seed 42 and stays clean; step 0.6 scores higher (.936) but grows dark halo rings inside cells. Recommend the soft form as a second output mode at step 0.5 only; it is out of focus by look (lines about 3x wider) and continuous by construction, which the hard form is not.

tournament.notes: Verified: check reproduces (c0ratio 2.08, range -0.772..1, far 4e4 clean, 3D z continuity ok); speed 223 ns = 4.46x perlin2, M=2 172 ns; seed 42 at a 24-unit window keeps the net with an isotropic FFT ring and no repetition; compare at seed 42 gives web .921 / single .565 / mesh .955 at D=1.1 and .668 / .502 / .900 at D=1.8, matching the table; vol at seed 42 is the same thick-walled foam. Baselines from real nodes are crack nets with uniform edges and flat or pyramid floors at 10.6 ns AVX2 2D for the richest, so the win is on look, not cost. Flaws: kink at det=0 (max slope 677), aliasing below about 30 px per unit with a dotted 4x wide view, spiky relief, departure from true ribbons above D 1.6. Port risk: internal Simplex with analytic gradient and Hessian in 2D, 3D and 4D, the 4D kernel unwritten.
tournament.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not ported: 2D ~7, 3D ~12, 4D ~23. Basis: measured scalar 232.7 ns = 4.49x perlin2 and 409 ns = 3.8x perlin3 (perlin3 measured 107 ns), times handbook Perlin AVX2, times 1.4 because SIMD cannot early-out empty simplex corners. 4D assumes the 3D ratio.

artist-terrain.note: Seed 42 w24: closed net of curved Y-junction lines, isotropic FFT, no repetition; vol is thick-walled foam. c0 2.08 and max slope 672 are real costs for a heightfield.

artist-material.note: Reads as pool light immediately, with thin lines over soft fans. The 3D form is also a good bone sponge. Ignore the spiky relief, this is a light map.

voxel-engineer.note: Thumb truly reads as pool light, and the foam vol is good. Relief has needle spikes from the det kink. Est 7/12/23 ns.

maintainer.note: The best caustic image on the sheets: closed net of Y-junction lines over soft bowls, corr .92 to ray truth at D 1.1. Cost ~7 ns est, c0ratio 2.08 (creases), 4D only via torus. Ship with Steps int, no other enums.

graphics-researcher.note: A pointwise function that actually draws a pool caustic net with varying line brightness, verified against a forward ray histogram. The CausticMesh discovery (true cusped ribbons, corr .955) is the more novel result and should be its high-quality output.

creative.note: Reads at once as pool light. The volume is a lovely membrane shell. Relief is picket-fence spikes, but height is not its job.

master.one_liner: Inverts the gradient map y = x + a*grad(h) with a few damped steps and outputs log(1/|det J|), giving a soft-bright caustic network (cracked mud, pool light, cosmic web) from one smooth noise.
master.look: Verified in prototype. Closed polygonal net of bright soft filaments, each cell a dark gradient bowl with internal fainter folds, like pool caustics or dried-mud cracks with depth. Hillshade reads as cobbles or plated hide. Two octaves with a=0.12 gives a finer double-scale net. Good for water caustic textures, cracked ground, cell walls, foam, cosmic-web density.
master.algorithm: Zel'dovich or lens map: rays start at q and land at y = q + a*grad h(q). Intensity at y is 1/|det(I + a*Hess h(q))| at the preimage q. Pointwise: q=p; repeat M (3..6): g=grad h(q); q=lerp(q, p - a*g, 0.5). Then compute grad h at q and at q+eps*e_i (D+1 gradients), J = I + a*(g_i - g_0)/eps, det J by closed form (2x2, 3x3, 4x4 cofactor). Output Scale*log(1/(|det|+Floor)). Prototype: dyn_lens mode=29,A=0.2,M=3.
master.why_new: Unlike CellularDistance F2-F1 it has no lattice-cell convexity: the net bends, has unequal cell sizes, cusps and internal secondary folds, and line brightness varies continuously. Single-pass ridged noise has lines at zero crossings, not at fold catastrophes. Cannot be built from existing nodes because they have no Hessian or fixed-point preimage.
master.simd_plan: M + D + 1 gradients. Best with an internal analytic-gradient Simplex or Perlin (2D about 6 gradients, about 9 ns; 3D 7 gradients, about 25 ns; 4D 8 gradients, about 60 ns). With a GeneratorSource and finite differences multiply by D+1. 3D form prototyped with perlin3: the slice is a clean web. All straight-line maths.
master.continuity: C0: compositions of continuous maps with Abs. Kink along det=0, softened by Floor. Measured c0ratio 3.6 and max slope 305 per unit in 2D at a=0.2.
master.params: Strength a (hybrid; acts as water depth, must stay low enough for fixed point convergence, about a*max|Hess|<1.5), Floor (line sharpness), Iterations, Source or internal noise frequency.
master.risks:
Above the convergence limit (a=0.35 on 2 octaves in test) it turns to grainy chaos, so a needs clamping or an auto scale. Single-start inverse sees one preimage only, so brightness is not a true caustic sum where 3 preimages exist. It looks right anyway. Output is skewed; range normalised by measured constant.
[CausticFilter, nature-phenomena] Single back-map is approximate: it does not sum over all folded sheets, so cusps are not physically exact. FD step must be tied to source Feature Scale, or the result shows noise or aliasing. Range is heavy-tailed. In a 4D tile, full-D det includes curvature normal to the image surface, so it may not match the 2D look (untested). The prototype used central differences (11 evals), so the 9-eval form is unverified.
master.cost_note: With analytic gradients about 9 / 25 / 60 ns for 2D / 3D / 4D (M+D+1 gradients); finite differences over a source multiply that by D+1.
master.variant_notes: CausticFilter is the M=1 back-map form of this and adds a Plane mode that differentiates x,y only, so an animated 3D source costs 9 evals rather than 14.

queue.name: CausticWeb
queue.reason: Earlier proto is one of the best images in the catalogue: pool-light webs, stable in 2D and 3D slices (J2 top pick). Needs an amplitude clamp and a Hessian kernel. Decides the caustic family.

fold-caustic.look: As written (single sheet, independent Perlin noises): separate closed loops around flipped blobs on a soft mottled floor, with faint Perlin axis streaks. No net at any amplitude. Flipped output is a plain blob mask, Signed is a soft noise, iterations 2 to 4 give crumpled plastic with small loops rather than nested folds. Back mapped first (back=3, Simplex): a very different and good picture, long open curved silk filaments with tapered ends and soft fans, not closed cells. That form matches the histogram of its own warp at corr 0.93 for A=0.5 and 0.79 for A=0.8. The true 3D slice of the back mapped Perlin form is sparser, with loops.
fold-caustic.dims: 2D measured in both forms. 3D measured: single-sheet slices are stable under z and stay closed loops; the back-mapped 3D slice was seen once on the sheet. 4D not run for this field.
fold-caustic.range: as written -0.838..1.000 mean -0.412; back mapped -0.863..1.000 mean -0.617, over 8 seeds and offsets
fold-caustic.artifacts: As written: corr .59 at A=0.5 and .38 at A=0.8 against the histogram of its own warp. With iterations the chain Jacobian is dq/dy, so its Inverse output is the reciprocal of intensity, which likely explains the crumpled look (not separately tested).
fold-caustic.node_shape: Field = Free on CausticWeb: d independent noises instead of the gradient of one. Everything else shared.
fold-caustic.port_notes: The formula is identical to caustic-web apart from a non-symmetric G, so a general 2x2, 3x3, 4x4 determinant replaces the symmetric one. The FD mode over any DomainWarp (WarpStrain) was not tested here and could still be a useful fold mask for existing warps; that is a separate and smaller question.

critic.params: A=0.8,out=1,back=3,noise=1,fq=0.8,eps=0.08 (back-mapped Simplex form; the as-written single sheet form is not worth shipping)
critic.notes: As written: drop, it is neither a caustic nor new. Back-mapped Free field: a look the catalogue does not have (warped ridged is marble, warped Simplex abs is worms), so it earns a Field = Free enum on CausticWeb, not a node. Cost is the issue: d independent gradient noises per step and a non-symmetric determinant, with the 3D form measured by the prototyper at 1180 ns scalar, so it is the expensive setting of the shared node. Use Simplex, not Perlin, to avoid axis streaks.

tournament.notes: Verified the as-written default speed 132.7 ns = 2.62x perlin2 and the images: as written it is separate closed loops around blobs on a mottled floor with Perlin axis streaks, not a caustic and not new, so that form is a drop. Back-mapped with a free field it is open tapered silk filaments with soft fans, a look the catalogue lacks (warped ridged is marble, warped Simplex abs is worms), and the 3D slice stays filaments. That earns a Field = Free enum on CausticWeb. It is the expensive setting: d gradient noises per step, a non-symmetric determinant, 3D measured by the prototyper at 1180 ns scalar; I did not re-run the back-mapped timing or continuity. Use Simplex rather than Perlin.
tournament.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE. As written: 2D ~2.7, 3D ~7.6 (measured scalar 126 ns = 2.45x perlin2, 371 ns = 3.5x perlin3). Back-mapped: 2D ~15 (measured scalar 492 ns = 9.57x perlin2, times 1.4 for no early-out), 3D ~35 with the Perlin form as prototyped (measured 1180 ns = 11x perlin3, three noises per step). The c0ratio and scalar_vs_perlin reported are for the back-mapped form; as written they are 3.66 and 2.45.

artist-terrain.note: As written: loops around blobs, a drop. Back-mapped free field gives open tapered silk filaments, a look the catalogue lacks; Field=Free on caustic-web.

artist-material.note: The sheet thumb is the back-mapped form: tapered silk filaments, closer to sun on sand than web is. As-written is a drop. Its vol is dull blobs. Belongs as Field=Free on CausticWeb.

voxel-engineer.note: As written: blobs in 3D. Only Field=Free silk is new, and that is expensive.

maintainer.note: As written: loops round flipped blobs with Perlin axis streaks. Back-mapped it is caustic-web at 2x cost. Not a node.

graphics-researcher.note: As written a drop; the back-mapped free field gives tapered silk filaments, a look worth a Field=Free enum.

creative.note: Thin silk filaments, arguably finer than the web. The volume is dull blobs.

master.one_liner: Jacobian determinant of a displacement field: bright one-line-wide caustic filaments with cusps where the warp folds, forming an organic cell network, at ~3x Perlin.
master.look:
Water-caustic / crumpled-foil networks: thin bright curves with cusps and swallowtails enclosing smooth dark cells; Flipped gives cusped organic blobs; with iterations the fold curves acquire nested sub-folds. Signed det alone is a smooth noise with unusual, 'sheared' statistics. Suited to water caustics, cracked glaze, cell membranes, lightning-ish filaments, and as a mask for where a warp over-folds.
[WarpStrain, graph-meta-filters] Proto sheetC m6: for a strong gradient warp, large organic blobs mark the regions where the warp has folded over itself (det < 0), surrounded by a continuous compression field; the warped texture inside the folds is the inverted, crowded part that gives 'Warped Cellular' its cut look. Det-1 is a smooth signed field (stretch positive, squeeze negative) that is itself a usable noise with strong spatial correlation to the warp. Uses: masks to hide or stylise warp folds, 'ink pooling' in the compressed zones of marble, density compensation for scattered features placed after a warp, FTLE-like stretch maps for stylised fluid textures.
master.algorithm:
W(p) = A * (n_1(p), ..., n_d(p)), d seeded internal gradient noises (Perlin with analytic derivative). G = [d n_i / d x_j]. Optional Symmetrise: G = (G + G^T)/2 (mimics the Hessian of a height field, i.e. refractive pool caustics).
  J = I + A*G ; det = det(J)   (2x2 closed form; 3x3 rule of Sarrus; 4x4 cofactors)
  Output enum:
    Density : out = exp(-det^2 / sigma^2)   (smooth, peaks on fold lines det = 0)
    Inverse : out = min(1, k / (|det| + eps))
    Signed  : out = det remapped
    Flipped : out = smoothstep(-s, s, -det)   (mask of folded-over regions)
  Iterations M > 1 (self-warp feedback): q = p; J = I; repeat M times: q = p + W(q); J = I + A*G(q)*J; then det as above.
FiniteDifference mode: accept any DomainWarp node as Source and build J from d+1 Warp() calls (forward differences).
master.why_new: Nothing in the graph can see how much a warp compresses area; det J is a first-derivative quantity of a vector field, unreachable from scalar nodes. It is cheap (d gradient noises) and gives caustic cusp geometry, which is absent from all existing nodes. Also valuable as a diagnostic filter on existing DomainWarp nodes (FD mode).
master.simd_plan:
d gradient-noise evaluations (~1.6x Perlin each), small determinant, exp. 2D ~3.5 ns (~3x Perlin), 3D ~11 ns, 4D ~28 ns (4x4 det ~100 flops, negligible). Iterations multiply by M plus d x d matrix products. FD mode: (d+1) x warp cost. Fully dimension-agnostic, tiles in 4D. Requires an internal gradient-returning Perlin (not a public node): the same utility the FlowEngine ideas need.
[WarpStrain, graph-meta-filters] 2D Warp() evaluations per output (4 / 6 / 8 calls in 2D/3D/4D), each a vector-returning call on the child warp (DomainWarpSimplex 2D ~2-3 ns), so ~12 / 40 / 100 ns before the child's own fractal octaves. Determinants are fixed FMAs; 2D stretch needs one Sqrt. Branch-free. Works in 4D because Warp() exists in 4D.
master.continuity: det is C1 for quintic Perlin (C2 noise); Density/Flipped smooth; Inverse C0 at the abs kink. Iterated version stays continuous (compositions of smooth maps).
master.params: Amplitude A (hybrid), Output enum, Sigma / Epsilon floats, Symmetrise bool, Iterations int (1..4), Source DomainWarp (optional FD mode), Seeded, ScalableGenerator, VariableRange.
master.risks:
Needs analytic-gradient noise plumbing; Inverse output has an unbounded peak and must be clamped/normalised by a measured constant; Symmetrised G is not a true Hessian (caustics look right but are not physically exact).
[WarpStrain, graph-meta-filters] Needs a DispatchClass that can call Warp() on a child DomainWarp; the typed GeneratorSourceT<DomainWarp> already exists for the fractal warps, so this is plumbing, not new infrastructure. The proto's Det output saturates at modest amplitudes because second derivatives of Simplex are large; LogDet or a Strength divisor is the better default. Niche compared with the other ideas, but very cheap.
master.cost_note: d gradient-noise evaluations (~1.6x Perlin each), small determinant, exp. 2D ~3.5 ns (~3x Perlin), 3D ~11 ns, 4D ~28 ns (4x4 det ~100 flops, negligible).
master.variant_notes: WarpStrain is the any-DomainWarp form of the same Jacobian, adding Stretch, LogDet and Compression outputs, usable to mask or density-compensate warp folds.

queue.name: FoldCaustic
queue.reason: det(I+A*G) of D gradient noises at 3.5/11/28 ns, the cheapest caustic (J4 top pick). Third leg of the caustic comparison; J2 expects smooth curves rather than cusps.

caustic-noise.look: Tangled thin smooth threads and closed loops, more wire or thread than light. No cusps, no polygon cells, no brightness hierarchy along lines. At Depth 1 it is blobs with rings, at 2 to 5 a finer and finer loop tangle. Ring spectrum at many waves adds long concentric arcs. Fold mode is a connected blob mask. By eye it sits next to Abs of warped Simplex raised to a power, a graph anyone can build today, and not next to the truth histogram.
caustic-noise.dims: 2D measured. 3D measured in two forms: z = time with phase speeds (w3=0, slices hold the 2D look) and true 3D sphere waves with 3x3 det (w3=1, slices softer and busier). 4D single sheet measured on the torus mapping with 16 waves: seamless, but bright blobs and threads.
caustic-noise.artifacts: Scored against the ray histogram of its own height: corr .41 and IoU .13 at D=2 with waves, falling from corr .61 at D=1. Best case corr .70 at D=0.8 on Simplex, where it is sparse blobs, not a net. Tried D 1 to 5, bandwidth 0 to 0.6, waves 6 to 24, Log and Fold modes, and both 3D forms.
caustic-noise.node_shape: Not its own node. It is CausticWeb with Steps = 0. The wave height is not worth a separate enum unless 4D cost matters.
caustic-noise.port_notes: Same determinant code as caustic-web. The wave sum has flat cost across dimensions and no lattice, which is its one real advantage. Far coordinates: check at 4e4 kept range and std, but the image there was not viewed. Float phase precision is a known risk for wave sums at large coordinates.

critic.notes: This is CausticWeb at Steps = 0, and it loses to Steps 1 (.832) let alone 3 (.921) at every Depth. It answers the family question: a single sheet det=0 does not read as pool floor caustics, it reads like pow(1 - |warped Simplex|, 8), a graph anyone can build today. The plane wave height costs more than Simplex, adds concentric arcs at many waves, and should not ship as an enum. Keep Steps 0 reachable as the parameter floor and nothing more.

tournament.notes: Verified speed 177.5 ns = 3.51x perlin2. On the same Simplex height at seed 42 the single sheet scores .565 / .133 and reads as worm loops and blobs with no cells, next to pow(1 - |warped Simplex|, 8) which a graph gives today. It is CausticWeb at Steps = 0 and loses to Steps 1 (.832) at every Depth. Keep Steps 0 reachable as the parameter floor; do not ship the plane-wave height enum, which costs more than Simplex and adds concentric arcs.
tournament.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE: 2D ~4, 3D ~5.5 (measured scalar 177 ns = 3.48x perlin2 at 12 waves, 265 ns = 2.47x perlin3 at 16 waves, times handbook Perlin). 4D ~10 is a guess from wave count.

artist-terrain.note: Worm loops and blobs, no cells; CausticWeb at Steps 0 and loses to Steps 1 at every depth.

artist-material.note: Worm loops that a graph already gives.

voxel-engineer.note: Worm loops, not caustics. The vol sponge is pretty but other nodes do that cheaper.

maintainer.note: Worm loops and blobs, no cells; pow(1-|warped Simplex|,8) from stock gets there. Drop or hide as Steps=1.

graphics-researcher.note: Worm loops and blobs; equals pow(1-|warped Simplex|,8). Steps=0 floor only.

creative.note: Worm loops with bright nodes, not light. The bony volume is better than the 2D.

members.note: Above about 1.6 it stays a clean net, departing from the true image. Capped at +-6, past which only dots are left and entry parity starts to fail.

members.name: Steps
members.note: 2 is the economy setting (.906 vs .921 at seed 42), 0 the single-sheet form; 4 adds nothing, 6 and up breaks lines into dashes.

members.name: Line Softness
members.note: Measured on the real node: aliasing has no threshold at 30 px per unit, the error of one sample per pixel against 16 is 14% of contrast at Feature Scale 84, 29% at 30, 57% at 10; Softness 0.5 gives 4%, 12%, 31%.

members.name: Gamma
members.note: 0.5 needs no Pow. Other values use Log2 and Exp2, since FS::Pow jumps at every sqrt(2) * 2^n.

plan_node.dims: Real 2D, 3D and 4D on the K1 Simplex Hessian, with both Lens Dims in 3D and 4D. GenTileable2D wraps with rounder cells and foggy patches.
plan_node.range: Native range is a floor to 1, the floor computed from Line Softness, Gamma and peak |det| measured at 10, 24, 70 for 2D, 3D, 4D at the default Depth. Default output -0.94..1, Free -0.99..1, clamped at Output Min at higher Depth.
notes: Avoid Perlin as the height: it shows axis streaks even in the true histogram.

Continuous with a very steep slope, 677 per unit in the prototype, which is why c0ratio read 2. The real node uses softness / sqrt( det^2 + softness^2 ), no crease and half the slope (fnlab check max slope 30.5 to 14.9 per feature in 2D), and fnlab check reads a step ratio of 7.8. fnlab seams still flags Feature Scale 40 (1 of 4000 in 3D and 4D, Free about 50); the flagged step shrinks with the window, so it is slope and not a jump. A texture, not a heightfield.
Corr/IoU against the ray histogram is not a quality judge: a Newton polish beat Steps 3 on the metric and looked worse. Judge by eye.

master.one_liner: Geometric-optics caustic intensity 1/|det(I + D*Hessian(h))| of a built-in random-wave height h, computed analytically pointwise: bright filament networks of pool-floor caustics with no simulation.
master.look: Thin bright filament network enclosing rounded dark cells, filaments brightest where they cross (cusps): classic underwater caustics / light through wavy glass / foil wrinkles; large D gives doubled, folded filaments; Fold mode gives a crisp organic cell mask with cusped corners.
master.algorithm:
Height h(x) = sum_i a_i sin(theta_i), theta_i = k_i*dot(d_i, x') + phi_i, with the same rotated direction table and hashing as WaveNoise (M ~ 8-16, Ring or narrow-band spectrum so filaments have one dominant scale).
Refraction/lens map: T(x) = x + D * grad h(x)   (D = Depth*(n-1), hybrid).
Jacobian J = I + D*H,  H = Hess h = - sum_i a_i k_i^2 sin(theta_i) d_i d_i^T.
Gen(seed,x):
  H = 0 (2D: Hxx,Hxy,Hyy; 3D: 6 terms; 4D: 10 terms)
  for i in 0..M-1: s = Sin(theta_i); c = a_i*k_i^2*s; H += c * outer(d_i,d_i)   (outer products of table vectors are constants: precompute d_i d_i^T table)
  det = det(I + D*H)   (2D: (1+D Hxx)(1+D Hyy) - D^2 Hxy^2 ; 3D: 3x3 cofactor; 4D: 4x4 by 2x2 blocks)
  Mode Intensity:    v = Min(1, Gain / (|det| + Eps)) * 2 - 1
  Mode LogIntensity: v = clamp(-Log(|det| + Eps) * Gain, 0, 1)*2-1
  Mode Fold:         v = sign(det)        (regions beyond the fold line, i.e. inside the caustic 'cells')
  Mode Height:       v = h normalised (the lens surface itself, for matching normal maps)
Animation: feed 4D w or Seed; Depth as hybrid gives caustics sharpening with water depth across the image.
master.why_new: Caustic networks require second derivatives of a smooth surface; no graph of existing nodes can produce the fold-line singularities (users currently fake it with Abs/Ridged which lacks the cusps and brightness law). Analytic Hessian from plane waves makes it as cheap as a noise and dimension agnostic.
master.simd_plan: Fixed M loop, per wave 1 Sin plus d(d+1)/2 FMAs into H; one small determinant; no lattice. Est. AVX2 M=12: 2D ~2.5x Perlin, 3D ~1.5x Perlin3D, 4D ~1x Perlin4D. 1/|det| guarded by Eps and Min; Log guarded. GenT with per-dimension det helper.
master.continuity: C-infinity away from fold lines; across fold lines 1/|det| diverges and is clamped by Min, giving a C0 plateau (filament core). Fold mode is a step function.
master.params: Waves M (int), Feature Scale, Depth D (hybrid), Gain, Eps, Bandwidth (0 = ring), Mode enum {Intensity, LogIntensity, Fold, Height}, Seed.
master.risks: Single-sheet approximation: intensity is evaluated at the surface point, not accumulated over the multiple surface points that land on one floor point, so beyond the first fold the picture is a stylised caustic (still looks right). Clamping makes filament width depend on Eps/Gain rather than physics.

queue.name: CausticNoise
queue.reason: Analytic Hessian of a wave sum, flat cost across dimensions (J1 top pick). Judges split on whether single-sheet det=0 reads as pool-floor caustics, so settle it side by side with caustic-web and fold-caustic.
